name: Modal Shift
description: Change the harmonic mode while keeping the same root note. Shift from minor to phrygian, or from a dark mode to an even darker one.
usefulWhen: The harmonic palette needs freshness without changing the tonal center
repair: Shift only one note at a time. A full modal shift on all pitched elements at once sounds like a different piece. Gradual modal mutation maintains continuity.
strudelHints: Change one note in the pattern (e.g., f → f# for dorian feel, e → eb for darker feel)
Shift one layer's pitch before shifting others

name: Detune Drift
description: Gradually detune a pitched element by a few cents over many cycles. Creates beating patterns against other elements, organic instability, and textural interest.
usefulWhen: Adding organic movement to static pitched elements, creating beating/textural effects
repair: Keep detuning very subtle (2-8 cents) for organic drift. Larger detuning (>20 cents) sounds intentionally out of tune.
strudelHints: Layer two sine waves at very close frequencies (e.g., note('d2') + note('d2').detune(4))
Slowly modulate pitch with .lpf() on a fast sine FM for microtonal drift

name: Registration Drop
description: Drop all pitched elements by one or two octaves. The music becomes darker, heavier, more physical. Or raise by an octave for an ethereal, floating effect.
usefulWhen: Need a dramatic shift in emotional character without changing the harmonic content
repair: After octave drop: add .hpf(40) to remove subsonic content. After octave raise: add .lpf() to control brightness.
strudelHints: Change note octave: note('d1') → note('d0') for drop, note('d1') → note('d2') for raise
Use .fast(0.5) for perceived octave-down on samples

name: Harmonic Reduction
description: Reduce harmonic complexity — move from chords to dyads to single notes. Strip away harmonic information to focus attention on timbre, rhythm, and space.
usefulWhen: The harmonic content is distracting from other musical dimensions
repair: Remove one note at a time over several cycles. The piece should become more focused, not emptier.
strudelHints: note('d2 f2 a2') → note('d2 a2') → note('d2')
Keep the root note until last — it's the harmonic anchor
